title: A Summer for the Garden
premise: Casper Dunmore has spent ten years exchanging letters with an anonymous correspondent she knows only as 'W', the one relationship she trusts because it demands no face. When W turns out to be Idris Vale, a disgraced investigative journalist hiding out in her late grandfather's old keeper's cottage next door, Casper must decide whether the woman she became through his words can survive meeting the man who wrote them. As the summer festival approaches and Idris's enemies close in on the story he abandoned, Casper chooses to stop containing her heart: she testifies beside him, exposing the town's buried injustice, and when the last train leaves on festival night, Idris stays, choosing her over escape.
about_author: Ada Oyelaran is a former archivist who grew up on the Atlantic coast and writes love stories where the landscape keeps score. She lives in a converted signal station with an unreasonable number of houseplants.

chapters.title: The Muscle of the Heart
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She finishes her novel, mails her annual letter to W, and recites her rules for containment. Beat: control as armor.

chapters.title: Smoke Next Door
chapters.summary: A stranger moves into the ruined keeper's cottage; Casper watches him from the dunes. Beat: intrusion of the unknown.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Casper finds a returned parcel addressed in W's handwriting, addressed to the stranger. Beat: suspicion sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: Idris Vale
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He recognizes Casper's name from a decade of letters and panics; he came here to disappear, not to be known. Beat: guilt and longing colliding.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Forced neighborliness; Casper tests him with a detail only W would know, and he deflects. Beat: cat and mouse, mutual attraction.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Logs
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Restoring her grandfather's lighthouse logs for the festival, she finds a 1998 entry about a drowned fisherman the town called an accident. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: What W Never Wrote
chapters.summary: Idris admits he's a journalist in hiding; he withholds that he's W. Casper offers her grandfather's logs for his story. Beat: intimacy built on a lie.

chapters.title: First Kiss at Low Tide
chapters.summary: A storm strands them in the lighthouse; the kiss breaks Casper's first rule. Beat: surrender, immediately regretted.

chapters.title: The Letter She Never Sent
chapters.summary: Idris finds her unsent drafts to W in the cottage's old desk and realizes she loves the correspondent, not him. Beat: jealousy of his own ghost.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Daughter
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She interviews the fisherman's daughter, Maren, and learns the town's founding families covered up negligence. Beat: justice stirring.

chapters.title: Compromised
chapters.summary: Idris's old enemies trace him to the coast; a threatening letter arrives. He pushes Casper away to protect her. Beat: sacrifice mistaken for rejection.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Planning the festival, she confronts the town patriarch Harlan Pike, whose family name is all over the logs. Beat: small town as pressure cooker.

chapters.title: Confession at the Cliff Edge
chapters.summary: Idris confesses he is W; Casper feels a decade of intimacy weaponized against her and walks the cliff alone. Beat: betrayal at its peak.

chapters.title: Burning the Letters
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She burns her half of the correspondence, then saves the last one from the fire. Beat: grief refusing to be total.

chapters.title: Maren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Maren agrees to go public if someone stands with her; Casper volunteers, outgrowing her invisibility. Beat: courage as choice.

chapters.title: The Story He Buried
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. He finishes the investigation he fled, choosing truth over safety, and sends it to a national paper. Beat: redemption through work.

chapters.title: Harlan Pike's Reckoning
chapters.summary: The story breaks; the town splits, Harlan's allies retaliate, and the festival becomes a battleground. Beat: justice outside the law, at a price.

chapters.title: The Last Train Before the Festival
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. With threats escalating, he packs to leave on the final pre-festival train. Beat: the old instinct to vanish.

chapters.title: Stay After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She meets him at the platform and asks him, plainly, to stay. He boards anyway; she walks home alone. Beat: heartbreak without retreat.

chapters.title: Festival Night
chapters.summary: The lighthouse is relit for the festival; Maren's testimony lands; Casper speaks her grandfather's truth before the whole town. Beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Man on the Dunes
chapters.summary: Idris returns, having sent the story and settled his debts; he brings the one letter she saved, unopened, and his own answer. Beat: return as proof.

chapters.title: A Summer for the Garden
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Epilogue in autumn: the garden they plant where the letters burned, her novel published with a dedication to W, and Idris, staying. Beat: love as a practice, not a containment.
